lines.text: Chapter five, section two. Stack-to-pot ratio, or SPR.
SPR is simply the effective stack divided by the current pot, measured at the moment you arrive on the street you are analyzing.
An SPR of one means you have exactly the size of the pot behind, so a single pot-sized bet gets you all in.
An SPR of four gives room for a check-raise or a small bet followed by a river shove, but not much more.
An SPR of ten or more is enough runway for full three-street barrels with reasonable sizing, which is where the leverage from prior chapters lives.
The reason SPR matters is that it directly determines how much equity a hand needs to break even in a stack-off.
At SPR one, calling an all-in requires only thirty-three percent equity, because you risk the pot to win three times the pot.
At SPR three, you need about forty-three percent, and at SPR ten you need almost fifty percent.
That climbing equity requirement means each player also stacks off with stronger hands as SPR grows, which cascades into every earlier decision.
Reading SPR before you plan your line is like checking the weather before you plan a road trip; ignore it and you will be miserable.
